promptLatex: Points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ lie on a circle in that order, with $\angle BAC = 40^{\circ}$, $\angle BCA = 35^{\circ}$, and $\angle ABD = 30^{\circ}$. What is the measure of $\angle CAD$, in degrees?
hintLatex: Convert each inscribed angle into the arc it cuts off, then use the fact that the arcs around a circle make a full turn.
The angle you want stands on the arc from $C$ to $D$ that does not contain $A$.
The arcs measure $70$, $80$, and $60$, so arc $CD$ is $150$ and half of it is $75$.
solutionLatex:
Each inscribed angle is half of the arc it intercepts, so the three given angles fix three arcs. $\angle BCA = 35^{\circ}$ stands on arc $AB$, so arc $AB = 70^{\circ}$. $\angle BAC = 40^{\circ}$ stands on arc $BC$, so arc $BC = 80^{\circ}$. $\angle ABD = 30^{\circ}$ stands on arc $AD$ — the arc from $A$ to $D$ that does not pass through $B$ — so arc $AD = 60^{\circ}$.

The four arcs around the circle make a full turn, so arc $CD = 360^{\circ} - 70^{\circ} - 80^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 150^{\circ}$.

Finally $\angle CAD$ is inscribed and intercepts exactly that arc $CD$, so $\angle CAD = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 150^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}$.
